ops.text:
A concurrent `task lint` run from a git worktree poisons the shared golangci-lint cache with worktree-rooted paths, and the repo's path-anchored gosec exclusions then stop matching — producing a phantom lint failure in the main checkout.

Hit 2026-08-19 while running two daemonkit lanes at once (one in /Users/yasyf/Code/daemonkit, one in a `~/.claude/worktrees/daemonkit/...` worktree). `golangci-lint run` in the main checkout reported:

    ../../.claude/worktrees/daemonkit/wf_96107be7-dc3-3/internal/wiregen/main.go:616:24: G703: Path traversal via taint analysis (gosec)

`.golangci.yml` excludes exactly this with `path: ^internal/wiregen/`, but that anchor cannot match a `../../.claude/worktrees/...` path, so the exclusion misses and the run fails. The file is identical in both checkouts and nothing in the diff touched it.

The trap: re-running `golangci-lint run` reproduces it exactly, which reads as a real, deterministic failure rather than a cache artifact. Only `golangci-lint cache clean` reveals the truth — after it, the same tree reports `0 issues`. There is no go.work, no GOFLAGS, and no GOWORK involved; `golangci-lint run` defaults to `./...` and never actually traverses the worktree.

Cost: a chunk of a session spent diagnosing a phantom failure, and it would have blocked `ccx vcs ship` (whose prek hook runs golangci-lint) with an error pointing at a file the change never touched.

Rule of thumb: when a lint failure names a path outside the checkout you are in, run `golangci-lint cache clean` before believing it — and avoid running `task lint` concurrently in a worktree and its parent checkout.
